messages:
Andrew: Quick follow-up from the GQ/MQ RFC — I ran a handful of long-seq workloads and saw a 12-18% p99 latency bump on the grouped-query path when `seq_len > 8k`. Want to sync on selector changes and a small refactor to make kernel choice less stateful.

Maya: Thanks. Can you paste the run IDs? I want to check if it's related to KV layout or batching changes.

Andrew: run: `job-20260319-gq-probe-3`. 3 warm runs, CPU traces attached in the CI artifact. It looks like the selector is choosing the GQ tiled kernel even when effective active tokens << tile size.

Sophia: That matches a microbench we saw — GQ tiled kernels lose out when sparse active columns drop below ~0.25*tile. We should add a lightweight occupancy check before locking kernel state.

Rahul: +1 on occupancy check. Tradeoff: we add an extra branch per request which could hurt hot-path latency. But we can memoize selector decisions per batch shape.

Evan: Proposal: keep selector pure and stateless, but expose a tiny hint field in runtime API: `workload_hint: {avg_active_cols:int, kv_hot_ratio:float}`. Runtime computes it cheaply from sampler and selectors stay deterministic.

Maya: I like the hint idea. Minimal API surface, ops teams can opt into emitting it. We should also add a fallback policy TTL so we don't thrash kernels on short fluctuations.

Andrew: Example TTL semantics: selector picks kernel K, record (K, shape) -> ttl windows of 200ms. If a contradictory decision appears within TTL, stick to current K unless delta > 20% throughput. Thoughts?

Sophia: Sounds reasonable. We should be explicit about metrics: use measured tokens/sec and memory peak. If memory overshoots or tokens/sec drops > 20% then force reevaluate.

Rahul: Pseudocode for cheap occupancy calc I shared in the RFC. Reposting small snippet here:

```
// run on batch collector thread
int avg_active_cols = sample_active_columns(batch, sample_rate=0.05);
float kv_hot_ratio = approx_kv_hits(batch);
if (avg_active_cols < TILE_SIZE * 0.3 || kv_hot_ratio < 0.5) choose(kernel_sparse);
else choose(kernel_gq_tiled);
```

Evan: Also: we need telemetry to detect selector thrash. Plan: emit `selector.choice` + `workload_hint` + `tokens_sec` every 250ms for a 5s window during canary. That should let us compute stability score.

Maya: infra-bot already ran the canary baseline yesterday, attaching the stability output. infra-bot: `canary-run-467` attached.

infra-bot: Canary canary-run-467 finished. Stability: 0.83, p99 delta vs baseline: +0.02s, sample_count: 64. Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/canary-run-467/.

Andrew: Good. Next steps I propose: 1) implement `workload_hint` emitter in the collector (opt-in), 2) add occupancy check + TTL glue in selector, 3) add canary telemetry dashboard, 4) a small e2e test in perf-suite asserting no >15% p99 regression across sample workloads. I'll open PRs for 1 & 2.

Sophia: For (2) let's keep the selector implementation pluggable (strategy pattern) so we can A/B a more advanced ML predictor later. No heavy refactor though — just a clean interface.

Rahul: I'll review PRs and run perf harness. Can we land the hint e2e behind a feature flag? want to toggle in prod quickly.

Maya: Yep. Feature flag + canary gate. Also add a small fallout plan: if stability score < 0.7 rollback kernel pinning and enable multiQ fallback.

Andrew: Thanks everyone — I'll split tasks and tag owners in the PR descriptions. If nobody objects I'll start the PRs today. :thumbsup:

Evan: ack. I'll draft the dashboard template and share a link in this thread when ready.

Sophia: Quick note — don't forget to update the eval harness for quality regression when we change quantized sparse kernels. Small behavioral diffs can be masked by batching changes.

Andrew: Good point. Adding eval step to the rollout checklist.
